title: Stella's Kitchen & Bakery In Downtown Billings Named Best Cinnamon Rolls In Montana By Business Insider - Montana Talks
content: I'm not typically a big sweets person, but when it comes to cinnamon rolls, I have a tough time passing them up. Perhaps it boils down to childhood memories of my Grandma and Mom baking homemade cinnamon rolls, or maybe it's just because they taste so darn good. Across Montana, from our biggest cities to our tiny towns, you'll find great cinnamon rolls. Oftentimes, some of the best places for this classic breakfast sweet treat are mom-and-pop style diners, cafes, and restaurants. Read More: 13,000 Daily Commuters Face Zimmerman Trail Detour In November Naturally, I had to click to see who nabbed the honor in Big Sky Country. And Billings area locals probably aren't shocked to learn that the publication said the best cinnamon rolls in Montana can be found at Stella's Kitchen & Bakery. Founded by Stella and Ziggy Zieglar (both deceased) in the early 1980s, the downtown Billings location at 2525 1st Ave N is a popular spot for breakfast, lunch, and brunch. The food quality, portion size, and price have never let me down.  And the cinnamon rolls... oh my. Stella's cinnamon rolls come in three sizes. The Giant is massive; it's easily more than enough for two people to share. The regular-size cinnamon roll is more like a large, and even their "mini" cinnamon rolls are huge. Staffers I spoke with said the classic with cream cheese frosting is their most popular seller. The caramel with nuts cinnamon roll is a close second. Often, you'll find seasonal specialty cinnamon rolls in their pastry case. Today, they had an apple cinnamon roll that looked amazing. You can order Stella's cinnamon rolls warmed up, served at room temperature, or take some to-go (so you can devour them on your couch in gluttonous privacy).

title: We Had An Incredible Turnout For Our Pink Out Bingo - kkam.com
content: On behalf of Townsquare Media Victoria(KIXS 108, KLUB Tejano 106.9, JACK FM, KQVT), we would like to thank everyone who made Pink Out Bingo on Tuesday, Oct. 27, at First English Lutheran Church such a meaningful evening. From our generous sponsors and table purchasers to everyone who purchased tickets and participated in the silent auction, your support helped make a difference for local families facing cancer. While the evening was filled with fun, prizes and community spirit, the purpose behind Pink Out Bingo was much bigger than a night of bingo. We came together to raise awareness about breast cancer and the importance of early detection, honor survivors, support those currently fighting cancer and their families, and raise funds for Crossroads Guardians of Hope. Crossroads Guardians of Hope serves eight counties, helping qualifying cancer patients who are actively receiving treatment with expenses during an incredibly difficult time. A cancer diagnosis brings so much to navigate, and financial stress should not have to make an already challenging journey even harder. Every ticket, table, sponsorship and silent auction contribution helped support this important local mission. We extend a special thank-you to our presenting sponsor, DeTar Healthcare System, for its commitment to this event and to raising awareness about breast cancer prevention and early detection. We are also grateful to our event sponsors: Formosa; Fountain of Youth Medical Spa; Royalty Nail Spa/Amour of God; TrustTexas Bank; Victoria Family Eyecare; VCS Communication Services; The First State Bank of Victoria; Scherer Kubota; WoodmenLife Insurance; VEA Health; and MW Rentals. Your generosity and investment in our community helped make this evening possible. Thank you as well to the local businesses that donated bingo prizes. Your contributions added excitement to the evening while helping support a meaningful cause. We are grateful to Sweet Fountainz for providing concessions, H2O Tea for sharing tea samples, and 5D Tavern for offering drinks for purchase. Thank you for helping make the evening enjoyable for everyone who attended. One of the most touching moments of the night was recognizing two local breast cancer survivors, Stephanie Schuckenbrock and Monique Garcia. McAdams Floral generously provided beautiful bouquets in their honor. Both women have faced breast cancer and are now thriving, offering inspiration and hope to others walking a similar path. In a beautiful gesture of paying it forward, Stephanie and Monique presented their bouquets to two women currently fighting breast cancer who were attending the event. That moment was a powerful reminder that no one should have to face cancer alone. Their stories also reinforced an important message: early detection matters. Mammograms can detect breast cancer before a lump can be felt or other symptoms appear. Stephanie’s annual mammogram detected a growth that was flat and would not have been discovered through a self-exam alone. Her experience is a reminder of why women should talk with their health care providers about their individual risk factors and recommended screenings. If you have been putting off your mammogram, please make that appointment. Finding cancer early can make a meaningful difference. Most of all, thank you to our community for showing up for one another. Breast cancer touches so many families, and behind every diagnosis is a person, a family and a story. Pink Out Bingo was an opportunity to celebrate survivors, encourage those still fighting, and remind families facing cancer that their community cares. Townsquare Media Victoria is proud to help bring our community together for an evening that combined awareness, compassion and action. Thank you for helping us support Crossroads Guardians of Hope and the neighbors who need it most.

title: Taiwan Semiconductor Flexes Pricing Power on AI's Frontline - MarketBeat

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company NYSE: TSM sits just beneath that ceiling. Investors evaluating infrastructure plays might start to notice a shift in how value is captured across the silicon ecosystem. Industry reports suggest TSMC is preparing a coordinated series of price increases across its most advanced packaging and fabrication services, testing the limits of its pricing power. If implemented, those increases would help the foundry pass its expansion costs downstream. To build modern AI accelerators, designers integrate high-bandwidth memory directly alongside compute dies. This integration requires highly specialized advanced packaging. TSMC's proprietary Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate technology is the industry standard for this process, creating a commanding position in high-end AI packaging. Traditional organic substrates struggle to provide the fine-pitch interconnects necessary for the terabyte-per-second memory interfaces demanded by next-generation graphics processing units. When processing large language models, data transfer speed is just as critical as raw compute power, making silicon stacking a core requirement. Recognizing this heavy reliance, TSMC could raise prices for its advanced packaging services by 10% to 20%. Downstream clients like NVIDIA NASDAQ: NVDA and Advanced Micro Devices NASDAQ: AMD have little room to negotiate. This inability to negotiate stems from the fact that new architectures, such as NVIDIA's Blackwell and Rubin, require extensive testing cycles. According to industry estimates, final testing for Blackwell takes about four times as long as Hopper, while Rubin could require up to seven times as long as Hopper. These extended cycles lock up testing capacity and equipment bandwidth across the foundry. Fabless designers find themselves prioritizing guaranteed production slots over unit costs. Adding to the packaging premium, wafer prices for TSMC's advanced 2-nanometer and 3-nanometer nodes could increase by an estimated 3% to 6% starting in early 2027. Successfully implementing these rate hikes across service lines without causing client attrition would demonstrate the outsized leverage in the semiconductor space. Pricing power directly influences profitability, but those premiums are meant to help offset heavy capital requirements. In the third quarter of 2026, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company reported a slight sequential dip in gross margin, landing around 66.4%. At first glance, the contraction might suggest pricing weakness, but it reflects the capital-intensive ramp-up of the new 2-nanometer node. Advanced packaging margins, which have traditionally hovered below the corporate average, are steadily expanding toward parity as the new pricing structure takes effect. The foundry maintained its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to an estimated $60 billion-$64 billion. Upstream equipment lead times for specialized packaging tools have stretched to around six to eight months. To bypass these delays, management reportedly placed equipment orders at existing prices without negotiating its usual vendor discounts. They prioritize scale over immediate cost efficiency because they have the leverage to pass these higher capital expenditure requirements directly to customers. The strategy centers on ramping monthly advanced packaging capacity to roughly 130,000 wafers by the end of 2026, with an eye toward 200,000 wafers by 2027. Passing the expansion costs downstream allows TSMC to maintain an exceptional net margin, currently hovering near 51.5%, even while financing one of the largest industrial expansions in modern history. Beyond pricing leverage, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing exhibits stringent corporate discipline when navigating high-profile partnerships. Recent negotiations regarding Elon Musk's proposed Texas-based Terafab project highlight this dynamic. Despite the potential for a large influx of capital and guaranteed capacity demand, the foundry refused to yield operational control of the facility. As a result, Musk indicated that Tesla NASDAQ: TSLA and SpaceX NASDAQ: SPCX will build and run the facility themselves. By walking away from a joint venture that compromises internal standards, TSMC insulates itself from high-risk external capital expenditure projects. This decision protects the proprietary foundry moat and helps to keep management focused on high-margin, fully controlled operations rather than diluting expertise across experimental partnerships. Controlling the intellectual property and operational efficiency of every fab remains a core tenet of the underlying business model. Investors assessing the current landscape should consider how these fundamental shifts affect valuation. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing is trading with a forward price-to-earnings ratio of around 28. Given the raised revenue outlook, with recent quarterly revenue expanding over 41% year-over-year to approximately $46.72 billion and earnings per share beating estimates at $4.60, the market appears to be digesting the ability to command premium pricing. Interestingly, institutional investors currently own about 16.5% of TSMC stock, leaving substantial room for broader potential institutional buying as the advanced packaging narrative becomes more widely understood. Investors might want to weigh the broader macroeconomic impact of these supply chain premiums. As fabless designers absorb higher fabrication and packaging costs, inflationary pressure on silicon eventually trickles down to consumer hardware. Subsequent price increases in end-market products could dampen broader consumer-level aggregate demand over a multi-year horizon. Cautious investors may want to monitor downstream hardware sales data to gauge whether end consumers can absorb rising AI infrastructure costs, while those seeking exposure to the technology sector's physical backbone might add TSMC to their watchlist as its advanced-node expansion continues. title: Over $250,000 raised at North Jersey’s first Komen breast cancer walk - New Jersey 101.5
content: What a morning at the South Mountain Reservation in West Orange, NJ. The sun was shining bright, but it was chilly when I got there around 8 a.m. on Sunday, Oct. 25. Cold enough where some people needed to wear gloves. But that chill didn't last long as more and more people arrived to what would be a very electrified event for the fight against breast cancer. The sea of pink across the field and between the tents was simply amazing. And that excitement continued throughout the morning as more gathered for the Susan G. Komen North Jersey MORE THAN PINK Walk. The first time in this area, but certainly not the last. In fact, the turnout was so large that the overflow parking lots were filling up. If anything, I think they need a larger space for next year. But that's a welcomed problem to have for an event like this. I myself was amazed by the turnout and it was so great to see. It was such an honor to be asked to host the walk. But what stood out the most was hearing the stories of survival. It was such a powerful morning, and I was so happy to see the sheer number of people who came out to help raise funds so we can keep the fight against breast cancer strong. Over $250,000 raised. Simply incredible! (see the recap video below). Komen.org is the place to go for all ways you can help support the cause and to get us that much closer to ridding this world from breast cancer. And remember, nobody should ever have to fight breast cancer alone. Despite delivering strong earnings and revenues that exceeded the Zacks Consensus Estimate, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing TSM, or TSMC, and Micron Technology MU have pulled back. TSM and MU have dipped 7% and 15.2%, respectively, so far this month, potentially offering investors an opportunity to gain exposure to the booming AI semiconductor market at more attractive prices. TSMC delivered third-quarter 2026 earnings of $4.60 per ADR, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 3.4%, while revenues surged 41.2% year over year to $46.72 billion, surpassing estimates by 2.4%. Riding strong demand for advanced chips, particularly for AI applications, the company expects fourth-quarter revenues of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion, signaling continued momentum into year-end. Micron reported an impressive fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 performance, with adjusted EPS of $33.42 exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 5.73%. Revenues soared 379.3% year over year to $54.23 billion, beating estimates by 6.33%, as surging AI infrastructure investment fueled demand for memory products, including high-bandwidth memory (HBM). While both companies continue to benefit from substantial earnings growth and the expanding AI ecosystem, broader concerns about intensifying Chinese competition in the memory market, rising U.S. inflation and interest-rate expectations and the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending weigh on semiconductor stocks. Against this backdrop, the recent pullbacks in TSMC and Micron raise an important question — could this dip present a timely buying opportunity and which semiconductor stock should investors prioritize? Let's delve deeper. TSMC is positioned to benefit from sustained AI infrastructure investment. In the third quarter, revenues surged 41.2% year over year, while EPS per ADR rose 57.5%, exceeding expectations. High-performance computing revenue rose 22% sequentially and accounted for 68% of total revenues, while advanced technologies contributed 79% of wafer revenues. The outlook remains encouraging. TSMC expects fourth-quarter revenues of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion, implying approximately 58% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. Its financial position is also robust, with $126 billion in cash and marketable securities at quarter-end and approximately $28.8 billion in quarterly operating cash flow. However, gross margin declined sequentially from 67.7% to 66.4% as 2-nanometer production ramped up. Overseas fabrication facilities are another source of pressure, with management expecting their gross-margin impact to widen to 3–4 percentage points over the next few years. Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results were strong, showing the earnings potential of the AI-driven memory market. Revenues soared to $54.23 billion from $11.32 billion a year earlier, while adjusted EPS reached $33.42, up from $3.03. Core Data Center revenue climbed to $18 billion from $1.58 billion a year earlier, reflecting surging demand for memory to support AI infrastructure. The company expects further acceleration in fiscal first-quarter 2027, forecasting revenues of $61.5 billion (+/- $1.5 billion) and adjusted EPS of $38.15 (+/- $1). This outlook indicates Micron's opportunity to capitalize on demand for high-bandwidth memory, server DRAM and other data-center products. Liquidity is another strength. Micron generated $43.97 billion in operating cash flow during the fourth quarter and ended fiscal 2026 with $73.48 billion in cash, marketable investments and restricted cash. However, the principal risks are the sustainability of exceptional memory pricing and earnings, the capital required to expand manufacturing capacity, and the cyclical nature of the memory industry. Micron's forecast of continued growth is encouraging, but it needs to be analyzed whether demand and pricing can sustain such elevated profitability as supply expands. However, Micron's unusually low multiple may reflect cyclical memory earnings and peak-profitability concerns. If investors had to choose just one, TSMC gets a marginal edge for its strong position in advanced chip manufacturing, diversified exposure to AI-driven demand across high-performance computing and other end markets and more established earnings visibility. Wei emphasized that AI-related semiconductor demand remains exceptionally strong, supported by accelerating adoption of agentic AI, open-source models and advanced computing infrastructure. During the Q&A, a Citigroup analyst questioned whether infrastructure constraints could affect growth. Wei indicated that AI accelerator growth could exceed the previously discussed mid-to-high 50% compound annual growth rate for 2024-2029. Wei also highlighted increasing demand for CPUs and networking chips. However, management clarified that CPUs remain outside its narrowly defined AI accelerator growth projections. Management now expects full-year 2026 revenue growth of approximately 44% in U.S. dollar terms, reflecting strong demand for leading-edge manufacturing technologies. For the fourth quarter, TSM projects revenues between $52.3 billion and $54.3 billion, representing approximately 14% sequential growth at the midpoint. Gross margin is projected at 65-67%, with operating margin at 56.5-58.5%. CFO Wendell Huang attributed margin pressure to the steep 2-nanometer ramp and overseas manufacturing costs. Meanwhile, Wei cautioned that rising component prices and macroeconomic uncertainty continue to challenge price-sensitive consumer markets. Huang reiterated the company's 2026 capital expenditure budget of $60 billion to $64 billion, reflecting its commitment to expanding manufacturing capacity. Management expects capital spending during 2026-2028 to be significantly higher than during the preceding three years. During the Q&A, a UBS analyst questioned whether equipment inflation would increase future investment requirements. Huang acknowledged rising equipment, material and labor costs but emphasized that long-term customer demand remains the principal investment driver. He maintained that revenue growth should outpace capital spending growth. Wei outlined an unprecedented global expansion involving nearly 20 manufacturing facilities under development, including 13 leading-edge and advanced packaging facilities in Taiwan. The company's 2-nanometer technology accounted for 8% of third-quarter wafer revenue. Management expects annual N2-family capacity to more than double in 2027, supported by smartphone and high-performance computing applications. TSMC also plans additional 3-nanometer manufacturing capacity in Taiwan while preparing its A14 technology for risk production in 2027 and volume production in 2028. Wei indicated that A14 customer engagement already exceeds comparable early N2 activity. Wei confirmed that TSMC is evaluating manufacturing expansion beyond Arizona, including potential opportunities in Texas. Responding to a JPMorgan analyst, Wei acknowledged discussions involving the proposed Terafab project. He clarified that any manufacturing collaboration would require TSMC operational control, although ownership arrangements remain under discussion. Meanwhile, Arizona's second fab is scheduled to begin 3-nanometer volume production in the third quarter of 2027. Huang expects overseas manufacturing to dilute gross margin by 3-4 percentage points during the latter portion of the company's five-year expansion period. Wei emphasized advanced packaging as another critical capacity priority amid increasing chip complexity and customer requirements. He reported successful production of five-reticle-size packaging solutions, with development progressing toward nine- and 14-reticle-size configurations. He identified CoWoS as customers' preferred packaging solution. During the Q&A, Wei also discussed collaboration with GlobalFoundries to support interposer supply. The chip builder reported a strong beat-and-raise Q3 on October 15, confirming that the AI capex spending spree remains full-steam ahead even as bubble concerns ramp up. title: Nvidia, Chipmakers Face Higher Costs? TSMC Reportedly Plans Up To 20% Price Hike For Advanced Chip Packaging - TradingView
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM) is preparing to raise prices for its advanced packaging process by 10%-20% as surging demand for AI chips strains production capacity, Taiwan’s China Times reported on Tuesday, citing supply-chain sources. If it goes through with the plan, it would raise costs for several chip firms, including Nvidia Corp (NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD). The move could also put further pressure on the prices of Apple’s (AAPL) iPhones and MacBooks, which have already seen price increases amid rising memory chip costs. TSMC is considering raising prices for CoWoS (Chip on Wafer on Substrate), its advanced packaging technology that integrates chips and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) into a single package. The report says the potential hike is being considered as demand for advanced packaging expands beyond GPUs to server CPUs and custom AI chips or ASICs, leading to capacity constraints. TSMC is continuing to ramp up its advanced packaging operations to meet demand, with monthly CoWoS capacity expected to exceed 130,000 units in 2026 and 200,000 units next year, China Times reported. TSMC is the world’s largest contract chipmaker, making advanced chips that power everything from AI data centers to smartphones. Its major customers also include Broadcom, Qualcomm and MediaTek. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment was ‘bullish’ for NVDA and AMD, and ‘bearish’ for TSM. TSM stock hit a record high on Oct. 5 but has since been caught up in the selloff in AI-linked stocks amid renewed concerns about the sustainability and returns of massive AI investments. Shares remain 40.5% up year to date. NVDA has declined about 11% from its record close on Oct. 6, but it has been up 16% year-to-date. “$CRWV $NVDA $TSM Ignore the noise from Musk. He's scared,” said a trader, referring to the SpaceX CEO’s bearish comments on the neocloud sector, which pressured several cloud and AI-linked stocks on Monday.
